newsitem.title: USA: German gets four years in jail for snake smuggling.
newsitem.headline: German gets four years in jail for snake smuggling.

text.p: A U.S. judge on Friday handed down the stiffest ever jail term for reptile smuggling, sentencing a German man to almost four years for conspiring to smuggle hundreds of endangered snakes and tortoises into the United States and Canada, the Justice Department said.

Wolfgang Michael Kloe of Raenberg, Germany was sentenced by Judge Ann Conway in Orlando, Florida, to 46 months in prison, after pleading guilty last October to conspiracy, smuggling, money laundering and attempted escape.

A second man, Simon David Harris of Blairgowrie, South Africa, was given three years probation for smuggling Madagascan tree boas and spider tortoises into Florida from Frankfurt, Germany in August 1996.

Trade in all of the animals smuggled -- Madagascan tree boas and ground boas, spider tortoises, and radiated tortoises -- is restricted under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species.
The animals were discovered when a Customs Service officer at Orlando International Airport felt something stirring inside Harris' suitcase, the Justice Department said.
Four others indicted with Kloe and Harris are outside the United States.
